# Texas college and training examples for career panels

Reviewed October 18, 2026. The new data module provides named, official-source examples for all 117 occupation panels. Each career receives one to three choices: 29 careers have one, 81 have two, and 7 have three. These are curated route examples, not a comprehensive college finder or a prediction of admission, licensure, employment, or earnings.

## Scope and interpretation

The catalog contains 111 separate program or award records, including 20 advanced programs reused from the existing education-cost evidence and one electrical certificate reused from education-route evidence. The original target of roughly 25–40 records was expanded to preserve distinctions among engineering majors, nursing levels, clinical credentials, and trades. No career receives an invented extra choice to satisfy a quota.

Institution-published facts are the program name, award, official URL, and any explicitly supplied duration or admission note. Career connections and the short benefit descriptions are editorial judgments about related study; the module labels them accordingly. An institution's listing of a program is not evidence that every graduate qualifies for every related occupation.

ACC's [2026–27 award catalog](https://catalog.austincc.edu/award-plans/degrees-and-certificates-listing-by-award-type/) distinguishes academic transfer awards from workforce awards. Transfer foundations require course planning with the receiving university; neither transfer admission nor major admission is guaranteed. The university examples are alternatives to investigate, not a claim that the particular ACC award automatically transfers into the particular university program.

Requirements panels remain authoritative for the full occupation route. Optional study for tattoo work, retail, customer service, stocking, delivery, cleaning, and other entry roles must remain visibly optional. An ASL interpreting program is not a Spanish interpreting program; a nurse aide course is not psychiatric technician certification; an RN degree is not an LVN bridge; and an occupational or physical therapist assistant award is not a therapist degree. No assistant award was substituted for its corresponding therapist profession.

## Integration contract

Only two new files belong to this change: dist/college-program-options.js and this document. Existing UI, engine, build scripts, tests, and source datasets were not edited.

The module exports:

- collegeProgramOptionsCheckedAt: catalog review date.
- collegeProgramCatalog: program records keyed by stable program ID.
- collegeProgramCareerMap: explicit occupation ID → program ID arrays.
- collegeProgramOptions(careerOrId): accepts an occupation ID or an object with id/careerId. Returns careerId, checkedAt, categories, optionCount, and note. Unknown IDs return no choices; no family fallback silently inserts a weak match.

Each category has id, label, and options. Each option carries title, school, location, award, url, routeType, benefit, duration, requirementsNote, tuitionURL, costEvidenceRef, sourceURLs, checkedAt, relationship, mappingBasis, and careerNote. Display relationship and the result note/careerNote next to the choices; hiding those fields can turn an optional or broader study route into a misleading qualification claim. Null duration means no verified duration is supplied, not that study has no duration. Some teaching sites are deliberately left at a regional level pending confirmation from the school.

The UI can show the named choice and one-sentence benefit first, with requirements and source details on expansion. This preserves the short, friendly guide while making depth available on demand.

## Costs and source freshness

No new tuition amounts were copied into the program module. Most ACC entries link to its current tuition schedule; most UT Austin undergraduate entries link to its tuition page. These are pointers, not total-program quotes. Additional institutional and course fees, residency classification, aid, living expenses, transfer credits, and pace can change the cost.

A costEvidenceRef is provided only for an exact existing named program: 20 educationCostEvidence entries and the ACC electrical certificate in educationRouteEvidence. The genericGraduate benchmark is excluded. Existing professional-program evidence retains its actual October 16 or 17 checkedAt date rather than being relabeled as newly reverified. Some professional links lead to the school's specific program cost or funding page because those are the evidence already reviewed; sourceURLs preserve those links. New program and current award pages were browsed on October 18. These dates describe the review, not a guaranteed institutional update cadence.

## Material source details and unresolved cases

- ACC's [truck-driving page](https://continue.austincc.edu/trucking) says five weeks in its description and four weeks in its summary. The module supplies no single duration and tells the reader to confirm the schedule.
- ACC's [medical-assistant page](https://continue.austincc.edu/medical) advertises as little as six to seven months and lists 720 hours over six to twelve months in its summary. The module uses the longer published range and preserves the qualification.
- The current ACC catalog marks its new Health Sciences–Vocational Nursing Specialty AAS as pending Texas Board of Nursing approval. The module instead uses the published [Vocational Nursing Level 2 certificate](https://www6.austincc.edu/cms/site/www/awardplans/programmap.php?aos=HESCI&ap=10323&yr=2027), which has separate program admission and licensure eligibility.
- The [Texas State entry respiratory-care BSRC](https://www.health.txst.edu/rc.html) is on the Round Rock campus. The module distinguishes it from the completion route for existing respiratory therapists.
- No occupation-specific Texas psychiatric technician program was verified in this pass. That career receives clearly labeled psychology and human-services study, with an explicit statement that neither is a psychiatric technician credential. This is a gap in the curated qualifying-program evidence, not a claim that no such program exists.
- Industrial design receives broader design and graphic-design examples, explicitly labeled as broader study rather than verified industrial-design specializations. Middle and high school teaching receive appropriate ACC teaching-transfer awards; there is no invented university subject/certification match.
- Cleaning receives management as optional preparation for supervision or business operations. Delivery and warehouse roles receive logistics as optional preparation for other responsibilities. These are not entry requirements or specialized cleaning/driving instruction.
- The inherited ACC electrical estimate remains only the listed 25-credit plan. Its evidence identifies an additional prerequisite ambiguity; this module preserves that limitation rather than turning the estimate into a guaranteed bill.

## Verification

An import and data-integrity check compared the module against all 117 exported occupations: all IDs mapped, no extra occupation IDs, no missing program records, one to three choices per career, all required presentation fields present, all cost references resolve to the named existing evidence, and unknown IDs return zero choices. This checks structural coverage, not admission eligibility or course equivalency. Public documentation was used; no accounts, applications, purchases, or real student records were created.

## Tuition-link integration follow-up

All example cards now have a tuition/fee link as well as the program link. Added official [TSTC tuition](https://www.tstc.edu/admissions/tuition/), [South Texas College tuition and program fees](https://catalog.southtexascollege.edu/tuition-fees/), [TXST One Stop tuition rates](https://onestop.txst.edu/cost-payments/cost-attendance/tuition-rates.html), and [Texas A&M undergraduate tuition calculator](https://tuition.tamu.edu/undergraduate) for the six records that originally only carried program evidence. The former TXST billing URL returned 404 and was replaced by the current One Stop page. Links expose each institution’s published pricing; they are not an individual bill or aid offer.
